channel.description: Latest articles from The Covington News (covnews.com)

item.title: Man dead after ‘apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound’ following hours-long standoff with officers
item.description: An unidentified man is deceased after an hours-long standoff with deputies from the Newton County Sheriff’s Office. The NCSO named an “apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound” as the cause of death.

item.title: Obituary: Jean Irene Jordan
item.description: Mrs. Jean Irene Jordan of Jasper County passed away on February 17, 2026, at the age of 96.

item.title: City of Covington celebrates Arbor Day
item.description: The City of Covington’s 34th Annual Arbor Celebration was held on Friday, Feb. 20.

item.title: Social Circle council ponders public assembly ordinance
item.description: The Social Circle City Council has sent their attorney back to the drawing board to tweak a proposed public assembly ordinance governing public property that council members saw for the first time Monday.

item.title: Covington Municipal Airport partners with Air Charter Advisors to expand business aviation access
item.description: Covington Municipal Airport (KCVC) has announced a formal partnership with Air Charter Advisors to coordinate on-demand private aviation services from its Newton County facility.

item.title: Covington City Council approves amendments for vendor permits
item.description: The Covington City Council voted unanimously to approve amendments for temporary commercial use permits at their Feb. 16 meeting.

item.title: CARROLL: A little dab'll do ya
item.description: A few months ago, we reminisced about cough drops, baby aspirin and various medications from days gone by. That opened the floodgates. Many readers shared memories of products we rarely see today. Let's take a trip down the aisles of the supermarkets of our childhood.

item.title: HARRIS: Financial Focus: Tax-saving moves you can still make for 2025
item.description: Tax season is upon us, and while April 15 may seem like it's right around the corner, you still have time to make some strategic moves that could lower your 2025 tax bill. Whether you're looking to reduce your taxable income or set yourself up for a more secure financial future, these options are worth considering.

item.title: NCS students Selected for GMEA District Honor Band
item.description: Newton County Schools has announced the students from across the district who have been selected to participate in the Georgia Music Educators Association (GMEA) District Honor Band — a distinguished ensemble representing some of the most accomplished young musicians in the region.

item.title: City of Porterdale approves 2026-31 Comprehensive Plan
item.description: In a unanimous decision, the City of Porterdale approved its 2026-31 Comprehensive Plan during a special-called meeting on Feb. 19. The city has been working on its latest Comprehensive Plan – which is a tool often used by local government officials to make future decisions – since April 2025.
